newsitem.title: TURKEY: Rebels attack unused Iraq-Turk oil pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Rebels attack unused Iraq-Turk oil pipeline.

text.p: Rebel Kurdish guerrillas have attacked a twin oil pipeline from Turkey to Iraq, causing an oil spill and fire but no interruption of Iraq's crude sales under a U.N. deal, oil officials said on Thursday.

They said militants of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) planted explosives on Wednesday night on the larger and unused one of the 986-km (616-mile) twin pipeline from Kirkuk oilfields to Ceyhan terminal on the Mediterranean.

"Iraqi oil is flowing normally. There is no interruption on that 40-inch pipeline," an official told Reuters, referring to Iraq's oil sales under the U.N. plan which allows Baghdad to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months from December to buy food and medicine.
He said the explosion occured at PSE-4 station near Sogutlu village in Mardin province, near the Iraqi border. "The explosion was at the 46-inch line," he said.

Provincial officials in Mardin said the fire caused by the explosion spread along the unused pipeline to the nearby Omerli town, but it was being extinguished by local fire brigades and those of the state company Botas, which operates the pipeline.
The pipeline has so far been attacked three times in the southeast by the PKK but Mardin governor Fikret Guven told Anatolian news agency that this was the biggest one.
Oil officials said the damage and oil loss could be known until the fire has completely be put out.
One official said a 135,000-tonne Bulgarian tanker, the Artega, had been loaded with Iraqi crude oil from the Ceyhan terminal and the tanker would sail to Bulgaria on Friday.
